_readme: MONEY-1379 — a PERCENTILE series from the GCP integration, scoped, compared
to a ceiling. Used by: workers-handler-time.
THE QUERY FORM IS DECIDED BY THE WIRE TYPE, and getting it wrong produces a
monitor that watches a series which cannot exist. `percentile(...)` / `p95:`
is the DISTRIBUTION query form. A DogStatsD HISTOGRAM (`|h|`) is aggregated
CLIENT-SIDE by the Agent into sub-metrics (`.avg`, `.count`, `.median`,
`.max`, `.95percentile`) and only those are shipped — the BASE name is never
a percentile-queryable series. monitor-latency-p95.json shipped
`percentile(last_1h):p95:stockbook.edgar.detect_latency_seconds{…}` over a
histogram for one release and evaluated against nothing; its
`_query_form_rationale` is the long version.
THIS TEMPLATE'S CASE IS THE SAME RULE FROM THE OTHER SIDE.
`gcp.run.request_latency.user_execution.p95` is a SUB-METRIC that Datadog's
GCP integration ships, already percentiled, out of Cloud Run's own bucketed
distribution. So it is queried with `avg:` over that ready-made series —
a space aggregator over one scoped value, not a percentile calculation.
Writing `p95:gcp.run.request_latency.user_execution` would ask Datadog for a
distribution that does not exist here, and the monitor would sit in NO DATA
forever — which, muted once, is indistinguishable from health.
THE UNIT IS MILLISECONDS. `gcp.run.request_latency.*` is in ms, so the 540
SECOND ceiling below Pub/Sub's 600 s ack deadline is written 540000, not
540. Measured 2026-09-11: last-hour p95 on stockbook-workers-prod was
93,695 (≈94 s), which is the sanity check that the scale is ms and not s.
A threshold written in seconds against this series is ~600x too low and
pages continuously; written in seconds against a seconds series it would be
1000x too high and never page at all.
SCOPE IS ALWAYS A NAMED SERVICE — never {*}. The same project runs two
algo-* services this repo does not own (see CLAUDE.md, MONEY-1379 ownership
boundary), and tiingo-realtime holds a WebSocket whose request latency is
the socket's lifetime, not a handler's.
_query_brace_rationale: `{{{scope}}}` is THREE braces on purpose: Datadog writes a scope inside
LITERAL braces, and dd_render's fill() matches `/\{\{(\w+)\}\}/g`, so it
consumes the inner two as the placeholder and leaves the outer one as query
syntax. The variable VALUE must therefore carry no braces of its own —
There is no `by` clause: the scope names ONE service, so a group-by would
produce a single group and a multi-alert monitor where a simple alert is
name: [{{env}}] {{label}}
_managed_tag_rationale: `managed-by:apply-perf-monitors` is its OWN namespace, distinct from the
apply-service-monitors.sh share. Reusing theirs would put these rows in
both scripts' listings, where each prunes what it does not recognise.
